decisions.reason: A low-pile decorative carpet carries little cost as a catalogue item, and one year of display has not yet resolved its uncertain value, so the option is worth keeping.
A hand-knotted wool silk carpet is a premium, likely made-to-order piece with low carrying cost whose value is still uncertain, so keeping the option makes sense.
This is one of several similar low-pile carpets in a broad range, which raises the chance of pruning, but there is no evidence yet that its value has failed.
A corner bench that builds on the established offer serves both residential and project clients, keeps the option cheap, and still has unresolved upside.
A low-pile carpet is cheap to keep listed and its uncertainty is unresolved, although overlap with the other carpets makes a later rotation possible.
A swivel shell chair line with several models represents substantial design investment and appeals across residential and contract markets, so the option should be retained while demand develops.
